notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 08/26/2025
Patient: Dillon Treutel, 79-year-old male

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 08/26/2025. The study evaluated sleep patterns and respiratory events throughout the night. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 53.1 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 15% of all events. Sleep was fragmented with frequent arousals related to respiratory disturbances. Oxygen saturation showed intermittent drops corresponding to apnea episodes.

Impression:
Severe sleep apnea with a significant proportion of central and mixed apneas.

Recommendations:
Initiation of positive airway pressure therapy and follow-up with a sleep medicine specialist for ongoing management.

notes.title: Sleep Medicine Consultation
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 07/17/2026
Patient: Dillon Treutel, 80-year-old male

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of obstructive sleep apnea with CPAP therapy.

History:
Mr. Treutel has been using CPAP therapy for obstructive sleep apnea. Despite consistent nightly use, he continues to experience symptoms suggestive of inadequate control.

Assessment:
CPAP failure: residual AHI 21.3 events/hour on CPAP at 11 cmH2O despite consistent nightly use.

Plan:
1. Consider alternative treatment options or adjustments to current CPAP settings.
2. Schedule a follow-up sleep study to assess efficacy of any changes.
3. Continue monitoring adherence and symptomatology.
4. Educate patient on potential next steps including possible use of advanced PAP modalities or adjunctive therapies.

Summary:
Mr. Treutel demonstrates persistent obstructive events despite adherence to CPAP therapy at 11 cmH2O. Further evaluation and management adjustments are warranted to improve sleep quality and reduce residual apnea events.
